sentiment.rationale: The full-year 2025 guidance was meaningfully raised: underlying EBIT guidance was narrowed from $2.0-3.5bn to $3.0-3.5bn, and underlying EBITDA guidance was raised from $8.0-9.5bn to $9.0-9.5bn. The improvement is organic, driven by strong volume performance, Gemini cooperation cost savings, and operational efficiencies across all segments, not attributed to one-time items or FX. Management expressed confidence in sustained demand and the trajectory of cost savings, supporting a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: Q3 2025 revenue was USD 14,206 million, down 9.9% year-on-year from USD 15,762 million.
summary.eps: Q3 2025 earnings per share were USD 69, down from USD 193 in Q3 2024.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 guidance refined: underlying EBITDA raised to $9.0-9.5bn (from $8.0-9.5bn), underlying EBIT raised to $3.0-3.5bn (from $2.0-3.5bn), free cash flow raised to $1.0bn or higher (from -$1.0bn or higher). Global container market volume growth revised to around 4% (previously 2-4%).
summary.margin: Q3 2025 EBIT margin was 9.0%, up 2.6 percentage points sequentially from 6.4% in Q2 2025, but down from 21.0% in Q3 2024.
key_risks: Ocean freight rates declined 31% year-on-year, reflecting ongoing market pressure.
The order book to fleet ratio for the container shipping industry is at 32%, the highest since the global financial crisis, posing potential future capacity challenges.
Increased trade imbalances leading to higher empty container repositioning and handling costs.
The IMO Net Zero Framework adoption was delayed by a year, losing momentum in global decarbonisation efforts.
Geopolitical environment remains fraught, with the Red Sea disruption expected to last for the full year.
key_opportunities: Gemini cooperation delivered cost benefits of approximately $225 million in Q3, with annualised savings of $720-950 million, exceeding original targets.
Strong volume growth in Ocean (7.0% year-on-year) and high utilisation of 94%.
Terminals delivered record-high volumes, revenue, EBITDA, and EBIT, with ROIC reaching 17.2%.
Logistics & Services EBIT margin improved to 5.5%, driven by operational improvements and cost control.
Continued strong demand, especially from China, with global container market volume growth expected around 4% for 2025.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management described 'strong execution across all businesses' and 'strong performance in the third quarter with good progress across all segments,' and raised guidance, reflecting confidence in the trajectory.
